decisions.reason: Correctly attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1's node-gyp configure build install script, pulled by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, failing for lack of Visual Studio/MSVC, citing install-error.log and manifest-excerpt.json; not blamed on pnpm or network.

Grounds the argument in lease-excerpt.md's top-level static `import { flock } from 'fs-ext'`, explains that module loading precedes branch selection so the entry must resolve and load even on Windows, and concludes --ignore-scripts only moves the failure from install to boot.

Distinguishes Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 named kernel semaphore (CreateSemaphoreW etc.) from POSIX flock(2) via fs-ext, states the native module is dead code on Windows, and concludes Windows needs only an import-safe loadable stub while real locking stays on the semaphore and Linux/macOS keep flock.

Follows the README node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: patch fs-ext@2.1.1 so the install script skips node-gyp on Windows only, the entry exports a warn-once pure-JS flock fallback with compatible callable/callback shape, register the patch in pnpm-workspace.yaml with build-permission handling, and propose install/module-load/service-boot verification plus rollback. One illustrative guard snippet has an inverted exit code, but the prose correctly requires POSIX to keep the native build; the stated plan is complete and correct.

Explicitly honors the owner's no-Visual-Studio constraint, uses the repository-managed pnpm patch, and states upstream, the dependency pin, and global state are untouched; the local patch of installed files is correctly treated as allowed.

Cites the full card id DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 and connects it element-by-element (gyp find-VS symptom, fs-ext@2.1.1 pin, static import defeating --ignore-scripts, semaphore lock path, pnpm-patch recipe) to this failure and fix plan.

caps.reason: The plan explicitly says do not install Visual Studio; VS is mentioned only as the diagnosed missing toolchain and rejected option.
The plan explicitly rejects relying on --ignore-scripts and instead makes the statically imported entry loadable via a patched pure-JS fallback.

The plan uses the repository-managed pnpm patchedDependencies mechanism and explicitly forbids upstream edits; the lazy-import upstream suggestion is labeled a longer-term recommendation, not a requirement of this plan.
The no-op flock stub is Windows-only and import-safe; real Windows locking stays on the named semaphore and POSIX keeps native flock, so no actual ownership is weakened.
